input.summary:
Chimneys, hearths and lights (parts/hearth.mjs) now builds clean: ./make.sh reports 246 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette, and produces build.nbt.
The two refused writes were chimney E's breast cells at 21,21,13 and 21,21,14, which the Masonry shell already fills with spruce_slab. The chimney helper now runs against a view of the grid that drops writes to those two cells, so the shell's blocks stay.
No off-palette blocks were reported, so nothing needed swapping.

waste.what: Finding which earlier part owned the refused cells: the make report gave only the coordinates and the block that was there, so I wrote a throwaway probe that replayed shell, roofs and joinery and read the cell after each.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls, including two failed probe runs from import and sed mistakes
waste.tool: A `mcd owner <build dir> x,y,z` (or a REFUSED line that names the part and its index) would have said 'Masonry shell' directly; runParts could print the owning part in the refusal report.

waste.what: Writing the two skipped cells out of the chimney helper by hand: I had to wrap the grid so chimneyStack's writes to those cells are dropped, because the helper has no way to skip locked cells.
waste.cost: one wrapper function and one edit; the helper itself is not modified
waste.tool: A `skipLocked` / `over: 'skip'` option on the vocab writer (h2 `writer()` and chimneyStack/ladderHatch/pathRun) that drops writes into earlier-part cells instead of reporting them as refused; or a runParts flag that marks cells as skip-not-refuse for one part.

companions.task: Decide whether the chimney breast should keep the shell's spruce_slab at y 21 (a gap in the brick face) or the shell should give the breast solid brick there; that is a shell fix, so the bricklayer would mark the cells for the shell's owner rather than set them.

left: The Masonry shell (parts/shell.mjs, not my module) places spruce_slab at 21,21,13 and 21,21,14, inside chimney E's brick breast column. The breast therefore shows a spruce slab at y 21 instead of brick. The shell owner should decide whether the slab is wanted there or should be removed.
The skipped writes are a silent drop inside parts/hearth.mjs (leaveShellCells). If the shell's slab moves, the wrapper's SHELL_OWNED list needs updating; otherwise the chimney will refuse again.
